name: Browny Orange
lede: Browny Orange modifies [[orange]] toward brown, and Paterson's dictionary already reaches for the exact phrase to define a bird's color.

sections.title: A phrase borrowed for a bird
sections.body:
As its own swatch, Browny Orange is recorded only by the xkcd 2010 crowd survey [1]. But Paterson's *A Dictionary of Colour* defines "oriole" as "a browny orange colour," using the exact words for the bird's plumage rather than entering Browny Orange on its own [2].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[xanthine-orange|Xanthine Orange]], only 3.0 units away and read as almost the same color [3]; [[ochre|Ochre]] sits close behind, duller by comparison [3]. [[dirty-orange|Dirty Orange]] is close too, almost the same color [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
This color appears in 116 of our 23,781 paintings, about 0.49 percent, more common than 60 percent of our named colors, as photographed [4]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, 1.7 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive, and it is most over-represented in Indian paintings, at 3.6 times the expected rate [4]. Inside a painting it plays an accent in 81 percent of its appearances [4].

The earliest match dates to a 1240 panel by Master of the Cross 434, 770 years before the xkcd survey; our archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [4].
